name: Geneva
tagline: Host a small private community without recreating Geneva's mobile network and member identity

pricing.notes: No stable public paid monthly tier was recorded; canonical amount is null.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Geneva, host a small private community without recreating Geneva's mobile network and member identity. The hard boundary is existing member network, native apps, chat, events, moderation, and hosted reliability, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a small private community, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control, without recreating Geneva's mobile network and member identity.
whatYouLose: existing member network, native apps, chat, events, moderation, and hosted reliability
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Geneva because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Discord Free
alternatives.desc: Private servers, channels, events and mobile apps, backed by the friend graph Geneva would otherwise make you rebuild.

facts.install: Hosted signup; use the web app or install Discord's signed desktop/mobile app
facts.dataFormat: Messages, server membership, uploads, and account activity live in Discord's cloud; the account data package is a ZIP containing JSON and media/metadata exports.
facts.gapVsPaid: Discord Free supplies private servers, channels, events, and mature mobile apps, but it is less purpose-built around Geneva-style community rooms, member profiles, and local social discovery.
facts.setupBlocker: Creating an account is easy, but moving an existing community still means recreating roles, channels, permissions, bots, and invitations.

alternatives.name: Element
alternatives.desc: Private Matrix spaces, rooms and encrypted messaging with proper mobile apps; the social discovery layer is thinner.

facts.install: Use a free Matrix account in Element Web/mobile/desktop, or deploy Element Server Suite on your own infrastructure
facts.dataFormat: Rooms, event history, account data, and media live on the selected Matrix homeserver; encrypted-room keys remain on clients and can be backed up through Matrix's key-backup system.
facts.gapVsPaid: Element gives private spaces, rooms, calls, and encrypted messaging, but Matrix terminology and a thinner social-discovery layer make it less immediately community-shaped than Geneva.
facts.setupBlocker: The clean hosted path is easy, but self-hosting the current Element Server Suite means operating a Matrix homeserver and its Kubernetes/Helm-based stack.

alternatives.name: HumHub
alternatives.desc: A self-owned private social network with spaces, profiles and activity streams; mobile polish is the tax.

facts.install: Use HumHub's paid hosted service, or install the Community Edition PHP package on a web server with MySQL/MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Profiles, spaces, posts, and configuration live in the HumHub SQL database; uploaded files live under the instance's uploads directory or configured storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: HumHub provides spaces, profiles, streams, and events under your control, but operating the server and accepting weaker mobile polish are significant downgrades from Geneva's managed apps.
facts.setupBlocker: The free route needs a PHP server, database, web-server configuration, cron jobs, mail delivery, backups, and upgrades before the first member joins.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Community plan plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Geneva in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a small private community, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control, without recreating Geneva's mobile network and member identity.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
